title: Expressions and linear equations
summary: Writing, simplifying and expanding expressions, solving linear equations and inequalities, formulas, and simultaneous equations.

cards.title: Algebraic expressions
cards.rule: A pronumeral stands for a number. \(3x\) means \(3 \times x\).

cards.title: Simplifying expressions
cards.rule: Only like terms (same letters, same powers) can be added or subtracted.

cards.title: Expanding expressions
cards.rule: Multiply every term inside the brackets by the term outside.
cards.tip: a minus sign outside changes every sign inside.

cards.title: Solving equations: one side
cards.rule: Undo the operations in reverse order. Do the same to both sides.

cards.title: Brackets and pronumerals on both sides
cards.rule: Expand brackets first, then collect the \(x\) terms on one side.
cards.tip: subtract the smaller x term, so the x stays positive.

cards.title: Solving word problems
cards.rule: Let \(x\) be the unknown, write an equation, solve it, then answer in words.
lines: "Triple a number, add 7, get 31": \(3x + 7 = 31\), so the number is 8
Rectangle 3 cm longer than it is wide, perimeter 26 cm: \(2(w + w + 3) = 26 \Rightarrow w = 5\), so 5 cm by 8 cm

cards.title: Solving linear inequalities
cards.rule: Solve like an equation, but flip the sign when you multiply or divide by a negative.
cards.note: On a number line: \(<\) or \(>\) is an open circle, \(\le\) or \(\ge\) is a closed dot.

cards.title: Using formulas
cards.rule: Substitute the values you know, then solve for the one that's left.

cards.title: Simultaneous equations: substitution
cards.rule: Replace one pronumeral with what it equals from the other equation.

cards.title: Simultaneous equations: elimination
cards.rule: Add or subtract the equations to remove one pronumeral.

cards.title: Applications of simultaneous equations
cards.rule: Two unknowns need two equations. Use a letter for each unknown.
lines: Adult tickets $15, child tickets $8. 7 tickets cost $77.
Substitute \(a = 7 - c\): \(105 - 7c = 77\), so \(c = 4\) and \(a = 3\): 3 adults and 4 children
